user: What should I check before making an international transfer?
answer:
Before sending an international (SWIFT) transfer, check the following:

- **Fees:** A SWIFT transfer has a flat fee of **EUR 15.00** plus **0.3%** of the EUR equivalent of the amount sent. For example, a EUR 1,000 transfer would carry EUR 15.00 + EUR 3.00 = EUR 18.00 in fees.
- **Intermediary charges:** Correspondent banks may deduct charges en route. Verta does not control these and does not refund them.
- **Timing:** SWIFT transfers usually settle in one to five business days. Submissions after 14:00 CET are processed the next business day.
- **Returned transfers:** If the beneficiary bank rejects the transfer, it is returned within five business days. Fees already charged are not refunded.
- **Limits:** A transfer is refused if it exceeds either your remaining daily or remaining monthly limit.

I also need to correct my previous answer about card payments. I said the documentation did not give the card fee percentage, but the tariff schedule does. Card payments carry a **1.2%** fee on the EUR equivalent, with no flat fee.

fragments.text:
Transfers
## Failed transfers
A transfer rejected by the beneficiary bank is returned within five business
days. Fees already charged on a returned SWIFT transfer are not refunded.

Verta tariff schedule
## Transfer fees by type
| Transfer type | Flat fee | Percentage fee |
|---|---|---|
| Internal | EUR 0.00 | 0% |
| SEPA | EUR 0.35 | 0% |
| SWIFT | EUR 15.00 | 0.3% |
| Card payment | EUR 0.00 | 1.2% |

The percentage fee is calculated on the EUR equivalent of the transfer amount.

Fee details
## How the SWIFT fee is composed
A SWIFT transfer carries a flat fee plus a percentage of the EUR equivalent of
the amount sent. Correspondent bank charges deducted en route are outside the
control of Verta and are not refunded.

Transfer limits
## How the remainder is computed
The daily remainder equals the daily limit minus settled outgoing transfers
dated today. The monthly remainder equals the monthly limit minus settled
outgoing transfers in the current calendar month. A transfer is refused when
it exceeds either remainder.
